prompts.prompt: Inspect emitted Venus instructions and Gem5 per-task ticks. Identify the dominant instruction family, dependency chain, and avoidable dynamic work; propose one falsifiable schedule change.
Reconstruct stage-by-stage live vectors including compiler temporaries and retained outputs. Shorten one live range or move one boundary before reducing vector length.
Map logical access patterns to continuous windows. Test whether layout pretransformation or in-register shuffle removes repeated short loads/stores without changing the ABI.
Search adjacent stages for a fusion that preserves the approved rounding, saturation, shift, mask, and output checkpoint semantics. Measure the fused candidate against the unfused baseline.
Separate configuration-derived values from runtime data. Precompute legal tables, indices, or layouts outside the task while preserving address non-overlap and configuration identity.

Starting from the numerical contract rather than the scalar control flow, derive a mathematically equivalent fixed-point formulation that better matches available fused, complex, mask, and reduction instructions.

Identify every payload-sized scalar loop in the hot task. Choose the largest regular dimension—RE, symbol, antenna, layer, code-block element, or a legal batch—and map it to long Venus vectors using continuous layout, masks, shuffles, reductions, or fusion. Keep scalar work only for configuration, address setup, or a measured unavoidable tail; confirm the transformation from emitted and dynamic scalar-versus-Venus instruction counts before ranking it.
Profile the full DAG critical path and data movement. Move or fuse exactly one boundary, then recheck every exposed intermediate and final output before ranking it.

If Gem5 passes and RTL fails, preserve firmware and case digests, find the first divergent instruction or address transaction, and create the smallest positive/negative probe for the syntax or ABI hypothesis.
